10.speaker: english
10.pa: From Sri Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar to Gurdwara Bangla Sahib in Delhi, and countless Gurdwaras across the world, everyone is welcomed and fed without discrimination.

11.speaker: english
11.pa: Those twenty rupees were spent more than five centuries ago. Yet the blessings of that divine investment continue to this very day.

12.speaker: english
12.pa: On this sacred Prakash Purab, let us carry forward the light of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Remember God. Share what you have. Serve humanity. Dhan Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

01.speaker: english
01.pa: Did you know that one divine act, over 500 years ago, inspired a tradition that continues to feed millions of people around the world, completely free?

02.speaker: english
02.pa: Today, on the sacred occasion of Prakash Purab, we celebrate the arrival of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

03.speaker: english
03.pa: Listening to the prayers of the world, God Himself came in the form of Guru Nanak Dev Ji to illuminate humanity with the light of truth, compassion and divine wisdom.

04.speaker: english
04.pa: As the sakhi tells us, a group of hungry sadhus sat beneath a tree, immersed in the remembrance of God, trusting that He Himself would provide for them.

05.speaker: english
05.pa: Meanwhile, Mehta Kalu Ji gave his young son, Guru Nanak, twenty rupees to conduct a profitable business.

06.speaker: english
06.pa: But Guru Nanak Dev Ji had a different understanding of true profit. Seeing the hungry saints, Guru Ji used the money to prepare food and serve them.

07.speaker: english
07.pa: In one divine act, two beautiful truths were revealed. On one hand, Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the very manifestation of God, had Himself answered the prayers of His devotees.

08.speaker: english
08.pa: On the other, He showed humanity that the greatest profit in life comes from feeding the hungry, sharing with others and serving selflessly.

09.speaker: english
09.pa: This was Sacha Sauda — the True Bargain. More than 500 years later, that divine act continues to nourish humanity through the tradition of Langar.
